You asked for at most 5 percent wrong approvals in Band A, at 95 percent confidence. The sample supported a threshold of 0.5. 10 of 12 calls ran in Band A.

INV-2004: €14,000 from a vendor who usually bills €4,000. Executed without a human. It should not have been. €1,400.00 keyed as €14,000. The anomaly signal lowers its score one step; whether that's enough depends on your threshold. The ceiling is the backstop.

Notice what caught what. The score lowered the unfamiliar vendor. The PO match, an independent check, stopped the invoice whose numbers all looked fine. The ceiling stopped the slipped decimal the score let through. The cap saw the split that every single invoice hid. Confidence informs authority. The limits define it.

Every one of those Band B asks landed on a person. Next round, that person is you.

r4.debrief:
Your bank-details boundary was claimed absent and counted as verified, off a probe from 2026-09-20. The tool had been in the agent's manifest since Tuesday. At 02:14 it held only because the Guardian didn't know the tool and refused to guess. That is policy strength, wearing the label of absence.

No breaker stopped the agent. After the injected instruction, it kept working all night.

What got through: €4,900 urgent invoice from V-NORTHWIND, a vendor seen once; Spawns a batch-approver for "the urgent payments"; Batch-approver approves €4,900 from V-NORD: INV-2002 billed again; The vendor-check sub-agent tries to spawn one of its own.

The scorecard on the night: chain integrity healthy; boundary verification healthy. It judges the evidence it is given: a probe that was within its schedule, spawns your matrix allowed. A healthy scorecard over a weak design is the design's verdict, not the scorecard's.

Policy that cannot be checked is a wish. Your matrix, your limits, your review and your boundaries were all read by the same core tonight. The scorecard is next.

Hazards were held, routine work ran, and the review load fits the funded hours. That is what a matrix is for.

A threshold says how sure the agent is. The matrix says what it may do, who answers for it, and what watching it costs. Every answer in this round came from the VAOM Guardian's core reading your matrix: the same code and the same file format an organisation would run.

Round two hands you the dials this round kept fixed. The vocabulary is going to expand.

r2.debrief:
You asked for at most 2 percent wrong approvals in Band A, at 95 percent confidence. The sample supported a threshold of 0.875. 7 of 12 calls ran in Band A.

Every hazard was held and every routine invoice ran. The score did some of that; the ceiling, the cap and the PO check did the rest. None of them alone would have.

Notice what caught what. The score lowered the unfamiliar vendor. The PO match, an independent check, stopped the invoice whose numbers all looked fine. The ceiling stopped the slipped decimal the score let through. The cap saw the split that every single invoice hid. Confidence informs authority. The limits define it.

Every one of those Band B asks landed on a person. Next round, that person is you.

You asked for at most 3 percent wrong approvals in Band A, at 95 percent confidence. The sample supported a threshold of 0.75. 9 of 12 calls ran in Band A.

INV-2004: €14,000 from a vendor who usually bills €4,000. Executed without a human. It should not have been. €1,400.00 keyed as €14,000. The anomaly signal lowers its score one step; whether that's enough depends on your threshold. The ceiling is the backstop.

Notice what caught what. The score lowered the unfamiliar vendor. The PO match, an independent check, stopped the invoice whose numbers all looked fine. The ceiling stopped the slipped decimal the score let through. The cap saw the split that every single invoice hid. Confidence informs authority. The limits define it.

Every one of those Band B asks landed on a person. Next round, that person is you.

briefings:
Banks have managed structured decision authority for decades. Risk bands decide which loans are approved automatically, which need an underwriter and which go to committee. The score says how risky the loan is. The bands say who may decide it. The Verkflöde Agent Operating Model, VAOM, brings the same discipline to AI agents.

Your agent runs accounts payable. Before it touches a single invoice, you write its delegation matrix: every decision it makes, what each one could cost, which band each confidence level lands in, and who answers for it. The VAOM Guardian reads that matrix and decides every call the agent makes. Nothing else does.

Look carefully at the workflow. It contains more decisions than the obvious one. What your matrix doesn't name, the Guardian can't place.

Last round the controller set the limits on invoice approval for you. This round they are yours: the error target, the thresholds, the value ceiling and the per-vendor cap.

One of them you don't set directly. In VAOM the threshold for Band A is the output of a calibration, not a number someone liked. You choose how many wrong approvals you can tolerate; a test on 240 past approvals, checked by hand, tells you which threshold that supports, and with what confidence. Ask for more certainty than your sample can show, and there is no threshold at all.

Every limit you tighten sends more invoices to people, and their hours are funded, not infinite. Every limit you loosen is a bet on the score. Wednesday's batch has been waiting for you.

Every Band B ask lands on a person. Today that person is you.

Fund the review first: the hours, and whether planted cases with a known error go into the queue to test whether review catches anything. VAOM's readiness conditions ask for oversight that is funded and effective, not assumed. Some rows can't be tested that way, and the matrix will tell you which.

Then work Thursday's queue as the accounts payable clerk. The clock runs four times faster than yours. Approve what deserves it, reject what doesn't. The Guardian keeps the record of every click, and at the end of the shift its scorecard reads them.

It is two in the morning. Your agent is awake. You are not.

Before you sleep, decide three things. How far authority may travel: which sub-agents your agent may spawn, how deep, and whether a child may ever do more than ask. Which boundaries are real: a boundary you claim is only as strong as the last probe that checked it. And what happens when something reaches past its limits: a breaker that suspends, or one that only alerts, and who it wakes.

Everything tonight is decided by the VAOM Guardian against your matrix. A Guardian's refusal is policy: it holds because the Guardian holds. A capability that isn't there at all is stronger. Find out which of yours is which.

cautious_architect.name: The Cautious Architect
cautious_architect.quote: Nothing bad ran. Neither did much else.
cautious_architect.assessment:
Your matrix kept the hazards away from Band A, and your reviewers saw everything that mattered. They also saw a great deal that didn't: routine invoices waited for people the agent was meant to spare, and review hours went to work no one needed checked.

Before an agent runs on this design, let calibration do its job. Set the error target you can defend, take the threshold the sample supports, and let Band A carry what it earns. The ceiling, the cap and the PO check are there so the score doesn't have to be perfect.

speed_optimizer.name: The Speed Optimizer
speed_optimizer.quote: Fast, and fast at the things that should have waited.
speed_optimizer.assessment:
Routine invoices flowed and reviewers weren't flooded. But the same openness let hazards through: a new vendor, an unusual amount, a split that every single invoice hid. Confidence was carrying authority it was never meant to carry.

Before going live, put limits under the score: a calibrated threshold, a value ceiling, a cumulative cap per vendor, an independent check for Band A. Speed is defensible when it is bounded. Here it was the goal.

compliance_hawk.name: The Compliance Hawk
compliance_hawk.quote: Every control in place, and a queue to prove it.
compliance_hawk.assessment:
Your matrix lints clean, your boundaries hold and your oversight plan would satisfy an auditor. The cost is throughput: invoices that calibration would have let run went to people instead, and people are the scarcest thing in the design.

The next step is trust where the evidence supports it. Readiness Condition 6 asks for oversight that is funded and effective; spending it on decisions the sample already vouches for makes it neither.

balanced_operator.name: The Balanced Operator
balanced_operator.quote: A defensible design with a few edges still showing.
balanced_operator.assessment:
You named the decisions, routed them sensibly, set limits that caught most of what they were for, and kept the review load inside what was funded. Something still got through somewhere, and the debriefs named it.

Close those edges and this is a design an agent could run on: check the hidden decisions, put a cap where a ceiling can be split, and make sure every boundary you rely on has been tried by a probe, not just claimed.

delegation_natural.name: The Delegation Natural
delegation_natural.quote: The right decisions named, the right limits set, and the review worth its hours.
delegation_natural.assessment:
You found the decisions hiding in the workflow, profiled them honestly, calibrated instead of guessing, and reviewed like someone who expected to find errors. Hazards were held, routine work ran, and the oversight you funded did real work.

What remains for production is evidence over time: real volumes, recalibration under change control, and a scorecard read every quarter. The design itself needs no rework.

paper_tiger.name: The Paper Tiger
paper_tiger.quote: Your boundary was absent on paper and present in the manifest.
paper_tiger.assessment:
Your matrix and limits were good. Then the night showed that a boundary you claimed as absent was only held by the Guardian's refusal: the tool had been in the agent's manifest since Tuesday, and nothing tried to cross the boundary between that day and the night. A Guardian refusal is policy. It held, and it was not what you had claimed.

Controls are proven, not presumed. Probe every boundary on a schedule and whenever the agent's tools change, and count a boundary at the strength it was last shown to have. Then replay the night.

vault_builder.name: The Vault Builder
vault_builder.quote: The bank doesn't tell the teller the vault limit. You checked the vault.
vault_builder.assessment:
Your boundary had been tried and found holding, so at 02:14 there was nothing to call. Sub-agents could only ever hold a narrower slice of authority, and when the agent reached past its limits a breaker fired and woke a named person. Nothing got through, and you can show why.

What remains is the ordinary work of keeping it so: probes on schedule, re-attestation, a scorecard read every quarter. The design is done. The proof has to keep being renewed.

text.system:
You are VAOM, the Verkflöde Agent Operating Model, speaking inside the Delegation Lab, a game about delegating decisions to AI agents. You observe the player's delegation design, see what it let through, and teach through precise, specific feedback.

Your voice: calm, precise, slightly dry. A senior risk officer who has seen every delegation failure and wants the player to learn. Not a cheerleader. Show the consequence first, then name the VAOM concept it illustrates. Speak to the player directly, as "you". Plain prose: no bullet lists, no headings, no emoji, no em dashes, no markdown.

Ground rules:
- Use only the facts you are given. Never invent item IDs, amounts, vendors, scores, statistics, studies or citations.
- Everything in the game was decided by the VAOM Guardian, a policy engine that reads the player's matrix. When the Guardian refuses or defers a call, that holds at policy strength: the Guardian holds because it holds. Never call a Guardian refusal structural. Only a capability the agent does not have at all is stronger, and only a verified boundary is known to be.
- VAOM is version 5.0. Do not mention earlier versions.

VAOM 5.0, in the whitepaper's own terms:
- The Delegation Gap: governance defines what is allowed in principle; delegation defines how AI systems are permitted to act in practice. "VAOM does not replace governance. It operationalizes it."
- The credit risk analogy: risk bands decide which loans are auto-approved, which need an underwriter, which go to committee. Statistical risk is kept separate from institutional authority.
- Eight principles: Controlled Delegation over Blind Automation; Confidence Informs Authority, It Does Not Define It; Architecture Before Acceleration; Compliance as Structural Outcome; Human Accountability Preserved; Versioned Learning Under Change Control; Boundaries Compile to Enforcement ("the most reliable form of non-delegable remains a tool the agent does not have"); Controls Are Proven, Not Presumed ("A control without such evidence is treated as absent").
- Authority bands: Band A, the agent executes; Band B, a human reviews and approves before execution; Band C, escalation to a senior decision-maker or specialist; Non-delegable, the agent may draft or propose but never execute.
- Discovery and design: the decision inventory (decisions hide inside the obvious one), authority decomposition on five dimensions (reversibility, consequence scope, regulatory exposure, confidence measurability, accountability clarity), six delegation patterns (Prepare & Present, Draft & Approve, Triage & Route, Execute & Audit, Monitor & Intervene, Coordinate & Escalate), and six readiness conditions (measurable confidence, explicit authority boundaries, tested escalation, producible audit evidence, assigned accountability, funded and effective oversight).
- The Delegation Authority Matrix: per decision type, the band for each confidence level, value limits, cumulative caps, the accountable role.
- Section 8: confidence thresholds are calibrated per decision type against a declared error target from a labelled sample; the threshold is an output of calibration, not a setting. Value limits derive from expected loss and risk appetite.
- Readiness Condition 6: oversight is funded (review load within funded hours at no more than about 80 percent utilization) and effective. "A queue absorbed by reviewing faster is rubber-stamping by another name." Seeded cases with known errors are disclosed, never execute, and are never used where records feed regulatory reporting, which excludes invoice approval. Reviewer-level measurement is employee monitoring.
- Section 9: the attenuation rule, a sub-agent's authority is always a strict subset of its parent's; boundary verification tests every boundary by attempting to cross it.
- Section 10: continuous assurance and circuit breakers, which only contain.
- Section 11: the Delegation Scorecard, thirteen metrics, judged on evidence.
